patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 6's new mechanical flows are supported by the cited patent text. The inner rod moves within the outer-rod channel and extends before the outer rod (c647dfbdca65ed580a7fe4455e897480; d856f17545af2880e13d21d88e18fca2); after piston contact both rods move in unison (e4a9b1922981551e62b6fb30a06518fc). The workpiece is contacted by the outer rod and removed through that interaction (530b093b1e33b5fe93c8faa1f1ca3c5b), while the description also says outer rod may press a part into place (c647dfbdca65ed580a7fe4455e897480). These ground the modeled motion/contact flows without asserting a quantified force. Prior pneumatic mapping remains carefully scoped to the preferred embodiment and externally applied pressure.

functional_completeness.rationale: The model represents supported telescoping motion and the external workpiece interaction in addition to the previously represented pneumatic behavior. No material omitted supported function is revealed by the reviewed passages; it appropriately leaves retract exhaust destination unspecified.

flow_consistency.rationale: F_MOTION is now represented by compatible mechanical_linear ports (IP_MOTION out and OP_MOTION in) joined once through IF_MOTION. F_WORK is represented by mechanical_force ports (OP_WORK out and LOAD_CONTACT in) joined through IF_WORK. These connections align with the described nested rod movement and outer-rod/workpiece contact. Pneumatic ports/interfaces remain type-consistent and the bidirectional port 128 accommodates exhaust during extension and pressure inlet during retraction.

claim_traceability.rationale: The new flow/interface statements cite detailed description passages and do not misrepresent them as claim limitations. Existing requirements retain explicit distinctions between claim-defined structure and preferred-embodiment behavior; no unsupported performance thresholds or obligations are introduced.

interfaces.rationale: Both previously disconnected flows now have existing endpoint subsystems, compatible typed ports, and referenced interfaces: inner/outer rod motion (IF_MOTION) and outer rod/workpiece contact (IF_WORK). Their mating endpoints are grounded by the cited passages. Each connection is recorded once.

textbook_application.rationale: The reviewed textbook guidance supports treating relevant external workpiece/supply entities as context and representing boundary-crossing interactions. It is modeling guidance only; patent evidence, not textbook text, grounds the specific motion and workpiece facts.

summary: Independently reviewed revision 6 against the actual cited patent passages. Both prior warnings are resolved: telescoping axial motion now has compatible linked mechanical ports between inner- and outer-rod subsystems, and the workpiece interaction now has compatible linked ports between outer rod and external LOAD. Patent passages explicitly support nested/relative rod motion, coordinated motion, outer-rod contact with the workpiece, and in some cases pressing the part. Pneumatic routing and bidirectional port 128 remain coherent, claim/embodiment distinctions are retained, and citations trace the new elements to patent evidence. No unresolved or newly introduced issues identified.
